title: Clamp two Mini-PROTEAN TGX gels in the electrode assembly: short plates in, arms shut
instruction: Load the two precast gel cassettes into the Mini-PROTEAN electrode assembly so it is ready for its run: one cassette on each green gasket, short plate facing in, pressed flat against the gasket and standing in the gel support so the short plate's top sits just under the notch, then swing each green clamping arm over its cassette until it clicks shut. Leave both cassettes clamped and let go.
context: Running an SDS-PAGE gel, alone or before a Western blot, is a daily bench step in molecular biology, biochemistry and clinical research labs, and the Bio-Rad Mini-PROTEAN Tetra is among the most common mini vertical cells. Loading the electrode assembly is where most failed runs start: a cassette put in short plate out, or not pressed flat, or an arm shut on a cassette that is not seated, leaves the inner buffer chamber leaking and the gel runs dry. The manual (Assembling the Mini-PROTEAN Tetra Cell) has the user hold both cassettes against the gaskets with one hand and shut the arms with the other, and warns against locking the arms before the cassettes are aligned at the notches. A cassette let go before its arm is shut tips out of its support. The finished state can be checked by eye and with a feeler gauge, and sealed or not is then visible when buffer is poured in.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; heights are over the table top. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left of their midpoint; bases at y +305 and -305 mm. (1) A Bio-Rad Mini-PROTEAN Tetra electrode assembly (the clamping frame of cell cat. 1658005), fixed to the table, centred at x 260 mm, y 0, its two green gaskets facing +y and -y, gasket faces 18 mm either side of y 0 (est). Its core is a U: two legs 40 to 52 mm either side of x 260 and a bottom bar to 18 mm, gasket over all of it, a notch at the top of each leg 82 mm up. Along the foot of each gasket a gel support: a groove 6 mm wide from the gasket face, floor 10 mm up, with a 3 mm lip to 16 mm. (2) Two green clamping arms, 195 mm long (est), 8 mm thick, 12 mm tall, 18 to 30 mm up, 40 g (est), each on a vertical pin at x 324 mm, y +26.6 and -26.6 mm (just outboard of a seated cassette's outer face). Each starts open, pointing straight out (+y, -y); shut, it lies along -x over the foot of its cassette's outer face. It swings freely; with a cassette pressed flat on its gasket, a cam resists its last 12 degrees (0.1 N m, est) and a clip catches it 2 degrees short of shut and holds it shut (0.1 N m, est); with no cassette there it swings past shut and never catches. (3) Two Bio-Rad Mini-PROTEAN TGX precast gels (cat. 4561033, 10%, 10-well, 30 uL), cassettes 100 x 80 x 4.6 mm, 30 g (est): long plate 2.0 mm (est), short plate with the 1 mm gel 2.6 mm (est), the short plate 70 mm tall, 10 mm under the long plate's top (est); friction 0.6 (est). Each stands upright in a white wet-storage rack block (30 x 120 x 20 mm, slot 6 x 104 mm, 15 mm deep) taped to the table: gel A at x 200, y +260 mm, short plate toward the robot; gel B at x 200, y -260 mm, short plate away. Each needs a quarter turn to go in short plate inward. A cassette let go in a gel support with nothing holding it leans out about 12 degrees onto the lip. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read from the poses of both cassettes and the angles of both arms. For each gasket, the best cassette on that side: Against: its face toward the centre within 1.5 mm of the gasket face at four points on the gasket legs (46 mm either side of its middle, the legs run 40 to 52 mm out; 15 and 60 mm up), tilted under 3 degrees from vertical, its width within 3 degrees of the gasket's line, its middle within 6 mm of the frame's middle along x. Short plate in: its short plate faces the centre. Seated: against, short plate in, and the short plate's top 0 to 4 mm under the notch (its foot on the support floor). Shut: the arm within 1.5 degrees of shut. Credit per side: 0.15 against with the short plate in; plus 0.15 seated; plus 0.20 if its arm is shut over that cassette (a cassette short plate out earns nothing on that side, arm included). Score: the sum over both sides, 1.0 for both seated short plate in with both arms shut. It counts only if, over the last 1 s, both grippers' finger zones stay 20 mm or more from both cassettes and both arms, and no cassette moves more than 2 mm or turns more than 2 degrees and no arm turns more than 2 degrees; otherwise 0. Latched 0: a cassette's lowest point more than 20 mm under the table top at any time (it fell off onto the floor). Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial: against, a 1.5 mm feeler gauge must not enter between cassette and gasket at the four points; tilt and line, a 3 degree wedge; short plate in, by eye (the shorter plate faces the core); seated, a rule from the notch to the short plate's top; shut, the clip has clicked and the arm lies flat on the cassette (a 1.5 degree wedge at its handle, about 5 mm at 195 mm); hands off, 20 mm spacer blocks and 30 fps video of the last second; dropped, by eye.
reset_notes: Open both arms straight out. Take the cassettes out and stand them in their rack blocks: gel A in the left block (x 200, y +260 mm) short plate toward the robot, gel B in the right block (y -260 mm) short plate away. Wipe the gaskets and the cassettes' outsides dry (no buffer reaches the grippers). One pair of gels serves many resets if kept wet in running buffer between trials (or use two spent cassettes with their gels in them); about 2 minutes.
fidelity: Rigid bodies: the gaskets do not compress and the 1 mm gel is part of the short plate. The clip and cam are one declared rule on each arm's hinge spring target (0.1 N m either way, only with a cassette flat on the gasket); nothing drives an arm shut or seats a cassette: the hands do both. The 12 degree lean comes from the groove and lip, not a rule. The 18 mm gasket offset, arm length, plate split, masses, torques and frictions are estimates (est).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (1441 steps); one arm idle: 0.5 (left idle), 0.5 (right idle)
